article_content: Michael Carrick believes Radamel Falcao will continue to find the net for Manchester United if he receives consistent opportunities in Louis van Gaal's starting lineup. The Colombian striker, who has only made nine Premier League appearances since his loan move to Old Trafford last summer, scored his second goal against Aston Villa on Saturday. Carrick expressed confidence that the former Atletico Madrid striker possesses the necessary attributes to secure a regular spot in United's starting XI, now that he has regained full fitness. Falcao headed in Manchester United's equaliser in their 1-1 draw with Aston Villa. The on-loan striker celebrated his goal in front of the travelling fans at Villa Park on Saturday. Speaking after the 1-1 draw at Villa Park, Carrick told MUTV: 'He's scored so many goals throughout his career, and you always have the feeling that he will score when he gets a chance. He scored a fantastic header again today [Saturday], and I'm happy for him.' 'Now that he's back from being sidelined, hopefully he can go on a scoring run for us, and we, as a team, can get back to winning ways and build some momentum.' Before the draw with Paul Lambert's side, United had secured six consecutive Premier League victories but now sit seven points behind Manchester City and Chelsea. Michael Carrick hopes Falcao will begin scoring regularly after his goal against Villa. Carrick celebrated with Falcao and Juan Mata after the Colombian's second goal for United. Despite Saturday's result, Carrick remains confident that the Red Devils will be in a strong position after the busy Christmas period. He added: 'Things are progressing well, although we were hoping for a better result [at Villa]. However, we didn't lose, and hopefully we can maintain that form over Christmas and emerge stronger in January.' United will host Newcastle on Boxing Day, followed by a trip to Tottenham on December 28 and a visit to Stoke on New Year's Day.

article_content: Happy New Year! Carl Azuz here, kicking off 2010 with CNN Student News. Today's headlines: First, the U.S. government has closed its embassy in Yemen due to security concerns. Officials suspect al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula may be planning an attack. This group also claimed responsibility for the attempted Christmas Day bombing of a plane headed to Detroit. The suspect allegedly hid explosives in his underwear, but the device malfunctioned. Questions remain about how the suspect bypassed security. A U.S. official cited human error. President Obama vowed to hold those involved accountable, though some critics feel his response has been too slow. The President also stated the suspect was trained by al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula. The U.S. military has been assisting Yemen in combating al Qaeda for some time. Barbara Starr reports on this: Barbara Starr reports on Yemeni forces conducting a raid against al Qaeda north of Sana'a. With U.S. support, including intelligence and training, Yemen is actively targeting al Qaeda. The U.S. military and intelligence community are analyzing all available information on al Qaeda in Yemen, with potential strikes involving U.S. missiles or aircraft. The U.S. and Yemen are seeking targets related to the Northwest flight 253 attack. Former President Bill Clinton's past efforts against terror were mentioned, highlighting a 2002 drone strike in Yemen that killed an al Qaeda operative involved in the USS Cole bombing. The U.S. continues to provide training, weapons, and intelligence to Yemen. Moving on, 'Is this legit?' Approximately 33% of the world's population is Christian, making Christianity the largest religion. Christians worldwide celebrated Christmas on December 25th, commemorating the birth of Jesus. Celebrations took place in Bethlehem and the Vatican, where Pope Benedict XVI led Christmas Eve Mass, briefly interrupted by a protester. In Iran, protests and violence marked a recent holy day. Demonstrators clashed with police, resulting in casualties. The Iranian government is planning a large-scale military exercise amid tensions surrounding its nuclear program, which it claims is for peaceful purposes. The U.S. Senate and House will meet to finalize a health care reform bill. Key differences exist between the Senate's $871 billion bill and the House's $1 trillion-plus version, particularly regarding the public option. Today's Money Word is 'depression,' an extreme economic decline worse than a recession. The U.S. avoided a depression but experienced a recession. Unemployment rose from around 5% in December 2007 to double that by last November. Kitty Pilgrim examines job prospects for 2010. President Obama stated the U.S. has avoided a financial collapse and that the economy is growing. However, businesses remain cautious about hiring. Economists emphasize that while the recession may be technically over, job growth is still lagging. Check out CNNStudentNews.com for free resources including show archives, transcripts, discussion questions, and downloadable maps. article_content: Amir Khan and his wife Faryal have welcomed their first child, a baby girl, on Friday. The former WBA and IBF light-welterweight champion and his wife, Faryal, have named their daughter Lamysa, an Arabic name meaning 'soft to the touch'. Khan, 27, shared the news on Twitter and later posted two photos cradling Lamysa. He tweeted: 'Faryal and I are delighted to announce the birth of our first child Lamysa Khan everyone doing very well, thank you for all your wishes.' A later tweet read: 'Mine and @FaryalxMakhdoom New born baby LAMYSA. Born on 23rd May 2014 at 4:05am £Blessed'. Khan and his wife met when she was a political science student in New York and became engaged in 2012. They married in June of the previous year at the Waldorf-Astoria hotel, before returning to the UK for another ceremony attended by more than 4,000 guests in Bolton, Amir's hometown. In an interview before his daughter's birth, Khan said he was ready to settle down and become a family man. He said: 'The past couple of years have been crazy - fighting, boxing. I've lived that single life, but it is the right time to settle down, be with my wife, and have my own little family.' 'Becoming a dad will help with my boxing, for sure.' 'The baby will keep me settled because there will be someone to look after. I'll have my wife and my baby girl to look after.' He insisted he wasn't ready to retire from boxing, saying: 'I will have a family to look after, so I will have to be much smarter.' 'I always said I would get out at 28, but I think I will be too young. I'm getting better, and I can see I'm getting more mature and stronger.' He added: 'I think it will be 30 plus. My wife won't be happy, but I can go on. Even the fights I've lost have been knock-outs, but I've hardly had any punishment. I've never been beaten up.' 'I will know when to stop when I am making mistakes, silly mistakes.' Khan and his wife, pictured in 2013, met when she was a political science student in New York. The couple married in June of the previous year at the Waldorf-Astoria hotel in New York before returning to the UK for another ceremony attended by more than 4,000 guests in Bolton, Amir's hometown.

article_content: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has stated his belief that the owner of the Washington Redskins is considering a name change due to the offense it causes to Native Americans. Goodell entered the discussion during a Q&A session with Dallas season ticket holders before a game between the Cowboys and Redskins. He mentioned growing up in Washington and initially associating the name with honoring Native American traditions. Goodell stated that Washington owner Daniel Snyder is 'way down the road' in considering a name change. 'But I think we also have to be sensitive enough to at least listen and try to see what it is we can do if we're insulting any element of our fan base, or non-fan base for that matter,' Goodell said. 'I think Dan Snyder is way down the road on doing that. I'm confident he's listening. I'm confident he feels strongly about the name but also wants to do the right thing.' The Redskins played their first game since President Barack Obama re-ignited the debate by saying he would 'think about changing' the name if he owned the team. Obama said, 'The name is just simply inappropriate. It is offensive to a lot of people.' Congressman Tom Cole, a Republican, has also called the name 'offensive.' The Oneida Indian Nation, which protested the name with a radio advertisement in Dallas, plans to meet with NFL representatives to discuss the issue. Before the game, a small group of protesters gathered near the stadium, holding signs that read 'Stop Perpetuating Racism' and 'Redskins (equals) 81 years racism.' Ray Halbritter, a senior leader of the Oneida Indian Nation in New York state, spoke at a symposium in Washington, DC, advocating for a name change. Yolanda Blue Horse, a member of the Lakota Nation from Dallas, said, 'I'm glad the president took a stand. If Dan Snyder wanted to honor Native Americans there's better ways to do that rather than Redskins.' One protester, Juan Mancias, drove from San Antonio with a flag of the American Indian Movement, stating he protested at a Cowboys and Redskins game at Texas Stadium in 1997. Jack Flack, a Redskins fan from Washington, suggested changing the name to Washington Senators, saying, 'I mean, if the president's weighing in, it's probably time for change.' However, Stephanie Smith, a Cowboys fan from Houston, said, 'It's a tradition. It's how it should be.' Cowboys owner Jerry Jones supported Snyder during the session with Goodell, stating, 'It would be a real mistake to think that Dan ... in any way has a lack of sensitivity regarding somebody's feelings. I can promise you that.' The name 'Redskins' was adopted by the football team in 1933 when co-owner George Preston Marshall renamed the Boston Braves. Many U.S. sports teams were named after indigenous peoples, but in recent years, these names have become more offensive.

article_content: In the United Kingdom, Davender Ghai, a 70-year-old Hindu man, recently lost his legal effort to gain the right to be cremated using a traditional Hindu open-air pyre. For many within the Hindu faith, this method is considered the most spiritually appropriate way of freeing the soul. Ghai, a well-known advocate for charities in Britain, contended that this practice is already implicitly permitted under current British law. His aim was to get official confirmation so such cremations could take place in the future without legal challenges. Back in 2006, Ghai put the law to the test by conducting a funeral pyre in Northumberland, a county in the north of England. While he faced no prosecution at the time, the Newcastle city council, where he resides, swiftly declared such funeral pyres illegal. Currently in India for medical treatment for debilitating health issues, including high blood pressure and diabetes, Ghai expressed his disappointment with the court's decision and announced his intention to appeal. His ultimate wish is to be cremated in the traditional manner when he passes away. 'I will continue to appeal until the very end, trusting that my final wish will be heard,' Ghai stated. 'An issue of this importance deserves consideration by the highest courts in our nation, and I will persevere until all legal avenues have been exhausted.' Presently, British law only permits cremation to occur within the confines of a crematorium. However, Ghai references the 2007 findings of Judge Andrew Collins, who deemed Ghai's case significant enough for a trial. Collins suggested that existing legal precedents don't automatically make open-air cremations unlawful and that this point could be debated in court. Those opposing open-air cremation argue that it is unhygienic and presents health and environmental dangers. Statistics, based on United Nations mortality rate estimates, indicate that in India alone, around 50 million trees are felled annually for funeral pyres, resulting in over 8 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions. Ghai maintains that the practice is a fundamental religious right for Hindus, who see open-air cremations as crucial for the soul's peaceful transition. The Hindu Council UK supports Ghai's position, referencing ancient Hindu texts that mandate cremation using wood-fueled fires in open spaces exposed to sunlight. 'We seek equality, not preferential treatment,' Ghai emphasizes on his charity's website, the Anglo-Asian Friendship Society. 'Hindus aren't expected to marry in a church, so why should Hindu funerals be forced into chapels that resemble Anglican churches?' Ghai also argues that permitting open-air cremations in Britain would alleviate financial burdens on Hindu families. Many British Hindus still favor the traditional funeral pyre and opt to transport bodies to India for the proper ceremony, a process that can cost as much as $5,000. Performing the ceremony in Britain would cost approximately a quarter of that amount, according to Ghai. The British Ministry of Justice has acknowledged Ghai's situation but doesn't offer much encouragement for his appeal. 'There are inevitably differing opinions on the appropriate ways to handle the disposal of bodies, stemming from various religious, moral, and ethical viewpoints,' the Ministry stated recently. 'There are currently no plans to alter the existing cremation laws.'

Antuk akeh ring pantaraning umat Hindu, tata cara puniki kaanggen sane pinih patut secara spiritual anggen nglepas atma. Ghai, sane kaloktah dados juru bicara antuk yayasan amal ring Britania, maosang praktik puniki sampun kabaosang kalugra antuk hukum Britania sane mangkin. Tetujonnyane inggih punika mangda molih konfirmasi resmi mangda palebonan punika prasida kalaksanayang ring wekas tanpa tantangan hukum. Duk warsa 2006, Ghai nguji hukume antuk ngamargiang palebonan ring Northumberland, silih tunggil kabupaten ring lor Inggris. Yadiastun dane nenten katuntut duk punika, dewan kota Newcastle, genah dane meneng, gelis maosang palebonan punika nenten kalugra. Mangkin ring India anggen pengobatan antuk pikobet kesehatan sane ngawinang lemet, rumasuk tekanan darah tinggi miwah diabetes, Ghai nguningayang rasa kuciwa antuk kaputusan pengadilan tur nguningayang tetujonnyane mangda ngamademang. Pangaptinnyane pinih untat inggih punika mangda ka kremasi nganggen tata cara tradisional rikala dane seda. 'Titiang pacang terus ngamademang ngantos puput, percaya antuk pangaptin titiang sane pinih untat pacang kapireng,' baos Ghai. 'Pikobet sane mabuat puniki patut kapertimbangang olih pengadilan pinih duur ring negara iraga, tur titiang pacang terus makarya ngantos margi hukum sami sampun katempuh.' Mangkin, hukum Britania wantah nglugra palebonan kalaksanayang ring jero krematorium. Sakewanten, Ghai nyihnayang panemuan warsa 2007 olih Hakim Andrew Collins, sane nganggep kasus Ghai cukup mabuat mangda kaadilin. Collins maosang preseden hukum sane wenten nenten otomatis ngawinang palebonan terbuka nenten sah tur pikobet puniki prasida kabligbagang ring pengadilan. Anak sane nyengkal palebonan terbuka maosang nenten hygienis tur ngwetuang bebaya kesehatan miwah lingkungan. Statistik, madasar antuk perkiraan tingkat kematian Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa, nyihnayang ring India kewanten, sawatara 50 yuta taru katembang nyabran warsa anggen palebonan, ngwetuang langkung saking 8 yuta ton emisi karbon dioksida. Ghai maosang praktik puniki wantah hak agama sane pinih utama antuk umat Hindu, sane nyingakin palebonan terbuka dados sane mabuat anggen peralihan atma sane tentram. Dewan Hindu Inggris ngadukung posisi Ghai, nyihnayang pustaka suci Hindu kuno sane ngamanatang palebonan nganggen geni sane kasuluh antuk kayu bakar ring genah terbuka sane keni sunar matan ai. 'Titiang ngarereh kesetaraan, nenten wantah katunas,' Ghai negesang ring situs yayasan amalnya, Anglo-Asian Friendship Society. 'Umat Hindu nenten kaaptiang marabian ring gereja, dados napi mawinan panguburan umat Hindu kapepet ring kapel sane pateh ring gereja Anglikan?' Ghai taler maosang palebonan terbuka ring Britania pacang ngicalang beban keuangan majeng ring kulawarga Hindu. Akeh umat Hindu Britania kantun ngutamayang palebonan tradisional tur milih ngirim layon ka India anggen upacara sane patut, proses sane prasida ngawinan biaya ngantos $5.000. Ngamargiang upacara puniki ring Britania pacang ngawinan sawatara seperempat saking jumlah punika, manut baos Ghai. Kementerian Kehakiman Britania sampun nguningayang kahanan Ghai nanging nenten ngicen pangapti sane akeh antuk pengadilannyane. 'Pastika wenten penampen sane mabinayan indik tata cara sane patut anggen ngicalang layon, sane mawit saking makudang-kudang penampen agama, moral, miwah etika,' baos Kementerian durung lami puniki. 'Mangkin nenten wenten rencana mangda ngicalang hukum palebonan sane wenten.'

article_content: The final Harry Potter film, the first in 3D, premiered in London. A key question: How many moviegoers will pay extra for the multi-dimensional experience? Despite being marketed as the ultimate viewing experience, interest in 3D films appears to be decreasing, with many fans preferring traditional 2D. When 'Avatar' was released in 2009, 80% of viewers opted for the 3D version. However, recent figures indicate a shift. Only 38% of the U.S. box office revenue for 'Pirates Of The Caribbean: On Stranger Tides' came from 3D tickets, highlighting a decline in popularity. 'Kung Fu Panda 2', released on Memorial Day weekend, also saw more viewers opting for 2D, earning it the nickname '3Disaster'. Box office figures suggest British audiences, like their American counterparts, are reluctant to pay more for 3D. Major cinema chains charge up to 41% more for 3D films, potentially costing a family of four an extra £11. Tim Richards, CEO of Vue, noted that negative feedback spreads quickly if the 3D quality is poor. In addition to the cost, many moviegoers report feeling unwell during 3D films, particularly in cinemas not designed for the format. Children can also find the glasses uncomfortable. Box office takings for 'Yogi Bear' were almost evenly split between 2D and 3D. 'Tangled' saw 44% of revenue from 2D screenings. These figures suggest that when factoring in the higher cost, more people may be choosing 2D.

article_content: Scientists have discovered that Sichuan peppers, a popular ingredient in China, contain a chemical that activates touch sensors in the mouth. For some people, the hotter the spicy food, the better. Yet, for others, the mouth numbness and tingling caused by eating chillies is simply painful. What causes this sensation, and why does it vary from person to person? Previous research suggested that chillies contain chemicals activating hot and cold sensors in the mouth. However, new research from University College London has discovered sanshool, another chemical capable of activating touch sensors. Sanshool, found in Sichuan peppers, can access parts of the lips connected to the brain area associated with touch. Study co-author Nobuhiro Hagura, a cognitive neuroscientist at the university, admits uncertainty about the exact mechanism. Sichuan peppers, also known as zanthoxylum piperitum, are primarily found in China and across the Himalayas. They are a common ingredient in spicy Chinese cuisine and are known for causing tingling lips and a numbing mouth sensation. The authors compare this sensation to the feeling of a mild electrical current. Chillies, part of the capsicum family, contain capsaicinoids like capsaicin. These chemicals activate the parts of the tongue that determine hot or cold sensations. Sichuan peppers additionally contain sanshool, activating touch sensors. During tests, Hagura applied Sichuan pepper powder to the lips of 28 male participants, all of whom reported numbing and tingling. Their fingers were then vibrated, and they were asked if the tingling on their lips felt faster or slower than the vibrations. Researchers found that Sichuan peppers created a sensation of 50 vibrations per second, the rate at which nerves sense touch. An American scientist suggests that personality might determine whether someone enjoys spicy food. Research at Pennsylvania State University explored the link between personality types and preference for spicy foods like chilli. The study found that people who seek adventure and intense sensations are more likely to enjoy spicy food than those who avoid risky situations. Their fingers were vibrated using a machine, and Hagura asked whether the tingling on their lips felt faster or slower than the movement on their hands. By changing the vibrational frequency, Hagura determined that Sichuan peppers created a sensation of approximately 50 vibrations per second. This is the rate at which nerves sense light touches on the skin. Hagura told LiveScience that these findings could help discover how taste affects the brain and why this differs among individuals. Earlier this year, an American scientist claimed that personality might influence the preference for spicy food. Pennsylvania State University's research examined the link between personality types and whether people enjoy spicy foods like chilli. It found that adventurous people who seek intense sensations are more likely to enjoy spicy food than those who avoid risky situations.

article_content: By Ryan Gorman PUBLISHED: 18:29 EST, December 31, 2013 UPDATED: 18:43 EST, December 31, 2013 Relentless rains pounding Hawaii’s ‘Big Island’ led to a truck being swallowed by a sinkhole on Monday. Velma Deluz was driving to work around 5:30 am when the road suddenly collapsed, swallowing her truck. She fortunately escaped without serious injury. The island received nearly half a foot of rain from the storm. Officials told local media that the accident likely occurred because a culvert beneath the road shifted, causing the road to collapse. SCROLL DOWN FOR VIDEO Swallowed whole: Velma Deluz's pickup truck was swallowed by a sinkhole, but she escaped without serious injuries. Ms. Deluz told KHNL about her terrifying experience. ‘When I made the turn, the road just sucked me right in,’ she told the station. ‘I fell in, and I tried to climb out the window because the truck fell on its side.’ The fortunate woman climbed out of the sinkhole and reached safety before another car drove by. She reported only minor rib injuries and expressed gratitude for being alive. Hawaii County Civil Defense spokesperson Darryl Oliveira attributed the collapse to a storm that battered the island for most of Monday. ‘It was spread out from Honoka'a to parts of Puna, pretty widespread windward side,’ he told KITV, adding that the rains were ‘a big problem because of multiple landslides, a lot of debris, and runoff in different areas.’ He further explained to the Honolulu Star-Advertiser that ‘the rain had caused a culvert beneath the street to shift, which then triggered the roadway's collapse.’ Ms. Deluz unfortunately drove over the collapsed roadway but was fortunate to escape. News footage from the Big Island showed extensive flooding, mudslides, and debris across roads. ‘It's been a while since we've had such a heavy downpour with so much runoff,’ Mr. Oliveira told the paper. ‘The ground has been pretty dry for a while. It's been drier than normal, and now we're having heavier than normal rainfall.’ More than five and a half inches of rain was recorded at Hilo Airport on Monday, almost a full inch more than the previous record set over 60 years ago.

article_content: This is a look at some of the illegal goods for sale on a new black market website inspired by 'The Lord of the Rings'. Middle Earth Marketplace, named after the fictional world in Tolkien's novels, exists on the darknet where criminals use special software and Bitcoin to evade law enforcement. Currently offered are illegal drugs, guns, ammunition, and a knuckle duster stun gun claiming to deliver a 950,000-volt shock. Sellers and administrators use names like Gandalf and Bilbo from 'The Lord of the Rings' and 'The Hobbit', and the site uses images from the films. Middle Earth was established after the original darknet marketplace, Silk Road, was shut down by the FBI in 2013. Silk Road's creator, Ross Ulbricht, known as 'Dread Pirate Roberts', was convicted on drug and conspiracy charges. Prosecutors stated that he facilitated over a million drug deals through the site, earning about $18 million in Bitcoin. Middle Earth is one of several marketplaces that emerged after Silk Road's closure, and its use of 'Lord of the Rings' imagery seems to give it an edge. One item for sale is a 'knuckle-blaster stun gun', said to incapacitate with a 950,000-volt shock, selling for 0.222 bitcoins (around £32). A Glock handgun is on sale for over nine bitcoins (around £1,300), with two magazines and worldwide delivery. A cheaper Keltec 9mm handgun is offered for 7.27 bitcoins (around £1,060), described as 'reliable' after test firing. Various marijuana types are available for sale. Illegal manuals on hacking, bomb-making, and murder are for sale on Middle Earth Marketplace. One drug dealer in the Netherlands offers to send 1kg of cocaine within Europe. A kilo of cocaine is priced at 154.2 bitcoins (£22,572), and single grams are advertised for 0.36 bitcoins (£53). Ten grams of 'Amnesia Haze' cannabis are offered for 0.5839 bitcoins (£85), and five 'Orange Turtle' ecstasy tablets from the Netherlands are priced at 0.0898 bitcoins (£13). A U.S. passport card is offered for 4.49 bitcoins (£657). Pre-fabricated EU driving licenses sell for 4.49 bitcoins (£657), while a digital template for a UK driver's license is advertised for 0.063 bitcoins (£9). Launched in 2008 by Satoshi Nakamoto, Bitcoin's value peaked in November 2013, but the current value fluctuates. At the time of this article, a bitcoin was worth around £140, so fractions are used. Fake IDs, credit cards, and personal identification cards are on sale on Middle Earth. A vast array of fake IDs, from UK Driving Licences to American Express Credit cards, are advertised alongside books on illegal activities. Most transactions involve illegal drugs, from small amounts to kilograms. One administrator claimed that many Silk Road dealers have migrated to Middle Earth but that they draw the line at assassination services and child pornography. Ecstasy tablets are sold in packs of five. 9mm ammunition is for sale. Transactions use Bitcoin, and messages are encrypted to ensure anonymity. Bitcoin is legal, but its value plummeted after the Silk Road bust. Police are setting up specialist units to tackle darknet problems. In the UK, a team is hunting paedophiles using the darknet. In the US, a search engine is being created to root out illegal websites.
translated_content: Puniki pinaka panyingakan ring makudang-kudang barang terlarang sane kaadol ring situs web pasar gelap anyar sane kainspirasi olih 'The Lord of the Rings'. Middle Earth Marketplace, sane kaaranin manut ring jagat fiksi ring novel Tolkien, wenten ring darknet dija para kriminal nganggen piranti lunak khusus miwah Bitcoin anggen nyingkiring hukum. Sane mangkin kaadol inggih punika narkoba terlarang, bedil, amunisi, miwah bedil kejut buku lima sane ngaku prasida ngamedalang kejut 950.000 volt. Para pangadol miwah administrator nganggen wasta sakadi Gandalf miwah Bilbo saking 'The Lord of the Rings' miwah 'The Hobbit', tur situs punika nganggen gambar saking film. Middle Earth kaadegang sasampun pasar gelap darknet sane asli, Silk Road, katutup olih FBI ring warsa 2013. Pangripta Silk Road, Ross Ulbricht, sane kasub dados 'Dread Pirate Roberts', katuduh ring kasus narkoba miwah konspirasi. Jaksa nyantenang indik dane ngalaksanayang langkung saking sejuta transaksi narkoba nganggén situs punika, ngamolihang sawatara $18 yuta ring Bitcoin. Middle Earth pinaka silih tunggil saking makudang-kudang pasar sane medal sasampun panutupan Silk Road, tur panganggénnyane ring gambar 'Lord of the Rings' kadi rasa ngicénin dane kaunggulan. Silih tunggil barang sane kaadol inggih punika 'bedil kejut buku lima', sane kabaos prasida ngicalang kakuatan antuk kejut 950.000 volt, kaadol antuk 0,222 bitcoin (sawatara £32). Bedil Glock kaadol antuk langkung saking sia bitcoin (sawatara £1.300), sareng kalih magasin miwah pangiriman ring sajagat gumine. Bedil Keltec 9mm sane pinih murah kaadol antuk 7,27 bitcoin (sawatara £1.060), kabaos 'terpercaya' sasampun pengujian. Makudang-kudang soroh ganja wenten kaadol. Buku pedoman terlarang ngenenin indik peretasan, ngardi bom, miwah pembunuhan kaadol ring Middle Earth Marketplace. Silih tunggil pangadol narkoba ring Belanda nawarang ngirim 1kg kokain ring jero Éropa. Sakilo kokain kaajengin antuk 154,2 bitcoin (£22.572), tur gram tunggal kaiklankan antuk 0,36 bitcoin (£53). Dasa gram ganja 'Amnesia Haze' kaajengin antuk 0,5839 bitcoin (£85), tur lima tablet ekstasi 'Orange Turtle' saking Belanda kaajengin antuk 0,0898 bitcoin (£13). Kartu paspor A.S. kaajengin antuk 4,49 bitcoin (£657). Lisensi nyupir Uni Éropa sane sampun dados kaadol antuk 4,49 bitcoin (£657), sawatara cetakan digital antuk lisensi nyupir Inggris kaiklankan antuk 0,063 bitcoin (£9). Kaluncurang ring warsa 2008 olih Satoshi Nakamoto, nilai Bitcoin ngancik ring puncaknyane ring bulan Nopember 2013, nanging mangkin harganyane sawatara £140, dadosnyane pecahan kaanggen. KTP palsu, kartu kredit, miwah kartu identifikasi diri kaadol ring Middle Earth. article_content: Following an incident where a police dog fell from the top of a building, an official inquiry has begun. The dog, named Baron, was a five-year-old German Shepherd serving with Essex Police. He was participating in a training drill with his handler when the tragic accident occurred in Danbury yesterday morning. Reports indicate Baron suffered substantial injuries after the fall from a flat roof. The loyal companion, known for his success in helping with numerous arrests, was immediately taken to a local veterinary clinic. Sadly, due to the severity of his injuries, he was euthanized. Essex Police have formally announced that a full investigation is underway to determine the exact circumstances of Baron’s untimely passing. A police spokesperson shared that Baron’s handler and their family are deeply affected by this loss. Superintendent Steve Johnson expressed his condolences, stating: 'This is a truly heartbreaking situation. Having been a part of the dog unit, I understand the powerful connection between an officer and their canine partner. While they are working animals, they also become cherished members of the officer’s household.'

Ipun sareng ring latihan sareng pangempon ipun rikala kejadian sane ngedihin puniki wenten ring Danbury dibi semengan. 'Laporan maosang Baron ngamolihang tatu sane ageng sesampune ulung saking atap datar. Asu sane setia puniki, kaloktah antuk kasuksman ipun ring ngewantu akeh panangkepan, gelis kabakta ka klinik hewan lokal. Santukan sanget tatu ipun, ipun katunasin nyawa ipun. 'Pulisi Essex sampun resmi ngumumang penyelidikan jangkep kantun mamargi mangda prasida nguningin indik tatujon Baron padem. Juru bicara pulisi maosang pangempon Baron lan kulawarga ipun sanget sedih santukan kapatian puniki.' Yadiastun ipun asu sane magae, ipun taler dados wagian kulawarga sane kasayangang.'

article_content: A recent poll indicates that more than twice as many voters trust the Conservative party over Labour regarding economic management. Ipsos Mori's polling reveals that the proportion of voters who believe the Conservative party, led by David Cameron, has the most effective economic policies has significantly increased from 35% to 45% over the past six months. This figure is 25% higher than those who favor Ed Miliband's Labour party on economic matters. However, the Conservative party has lost its lead in public opinion on European and immigration policies, with UKIP now considered the most capable party to address these issues. Concurrently, the percentage of voters identifying immigration as their top concern has doubled since 2010, reaching 30%. While the Conservatives maintain a clear advantage on the economy, which is voters' primary concern, they trail behind on immigration and healthcare. The economy continues to be the most pressing issue for voters, ahead of immigration, healthcare, and education. The same poll showed that the economy is a decisive factor for the public when choosing who to vote for. Economic management is considered the most critical issue by 31% of the public, closely followed by immigration and healthcare. Immigration has risen from fourth to second place among voters' top concerns, while health and education have fallen to third and fourth, respectively. Welfare is now the fifth most important issue, surpassing tax, crime, and unemployment. Although the Conservative party is viewed as the most competent on the economy, it lags narrowly behind UKIP on immigration and significantly behind Labour on healthcare. The proportion of voters who believe UKIP has the best immigration policies has almost doubled in the past year. In September of the previous year, 11% supported Nigel Farage's party on immigration policies; this has surged to 20%. Only 19% believe the Conservatives have the best policies, a decrease of three percent. Labour receives 18% support on this issue. Ed Miliband's Labour party is favored by voters on health and education, but David Cameron's Conservative party is significantly ahead on the economy. UKIP also leads on European policies, with just under a quarter supporting Nigel Farage's stance. Only one in five support David Cameron on EU matters. Labour leads on three of the top five issues: health, education, and welfare. Gideon Skinner, of Ipsos MORI, commented: 'We’re in the extraordinary situation of having three issues tied at the top as most important to the public, and a different party making the running on each — the Conservatives on the economy, UKIP on immigration, and Labour on healthcare. 'Therefore, all parties have their key issue, but going into party conferences season, there is still everything to play for.' Last week, the same pollsters found that the Conservatives had regained the lead in polls ahead of Labour, just eight months before the general election in May. The Conservatives were supported by 34% of those certain to vote in the upcoming general election, compared to 33% for Labour. UKIP received 15% support, and the Liberal Democrats received 7%. David Cameron's Conservative party has edged ahead of Labour just eight months before the next general election. This places the Conservatives ahead of Labour for the first time since December 2011 in the Ipsos MORI surveys. Nigel Farage's efforts to dispel the ‘wasted vote’ perception received a boost, as the number agreeing that supporting UKIP at a general election is a wasted vote has decreased from 57% to 50% since May. Over half (53%) of those surveyed said the eurosceptic party was raising important issues that other parties were not adequately addressing, and 14% said they would like their local MP to defect to UKIP.

article_content: According to data from the BMC's health department released before World Diabetes Day, six out of ten Mumbaikars have weight problems that increase their susceptibility to diabetes. Currently, 18% of Mumbaikars aged 18 to 69 years have either impaired fasting blood sugar levels (exceeding 126mg/dl) or diabetes, while an additional 16% have prediabetes. Dr. Daksha Shah, the BMC's executive health officer, stated that 'The risk of type 2 diabetes is greater in individuals who are obese or lead sedentary lifestyles, typically affecting those aged 35 or older. It elevates the likelihood of developing cardiovascular diseases, which contribute to nearly a quarter of all deaths in the city.' The proportion of Mumbaikars at risk of diabetes is substantial, considering the BMC's STEPS survey in 2021 revealed that 46% of residents were overweight (with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or higher), and another 12% were obese (with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher). Obesity was more prevalent among women. Over the past two years, the BMC has initiated a screening program for diabetes and hypertension, testing over 60,000 individuals each month at its facilities; approximately 50,000 receive free diabetes treatment. Screening of over 250,000 people at the diabetes and hypertension screening centers (NCD corners) in 26 civic-run hospitals since August 2022 indicated an incidence rate of 12%. The BMC's door-to-door survey of 130,000 people has found that 9% have diabetes. On Tuesday, Mumbaikars can receive complimentary testing for diabetes and hypertension at parks, railway stations, and malls. Dr. Shah noted that at least 50% of individuals with diabetes are unaware of their condition until diagnosed. 'It is crucial to be aware and monitor blood sugar levels regularly,' she added. Cardiologist Dr. Anand Rao commented that India has unfortunately become known as the diabetes capital of the world, a situation that is likely to worsen unless people improve their exercise habits and diets. 'The genetic predisposition of Indians to diabetes, combined with a preference for consuming overcooked food that is high in salt, excessively rich in carbohydrates, and deficient in protein, is a formula for lifestyle diseases,' Dr. Rao explained. Furthermore, many diabetes patients are non-compliant and do not consistently check their sugar levels.

Punika nginggilang potensi keni penyakit kardiovaskular, sane nyumbang kirang langkung seperempat saking sakancan seda ring kota.' article_content: Robert O'Neill, a former Navy SEAL, asserts that he fired the shot that killed Osama bin Laden and remains unconcerned whether people believe him. In an audio interview with Alex Quade, a freelance journalist and former CNN correspondent, broadcast on CNN's 'AC360,' O'Neill stated, 'The most important thing that I've learned in the last two years is to me it doesn't matter anymore if I am 'The Shooter.' The team got him.' He added, 'Regardless of the negativity that comes with it, I don't give a f***. We got him.' 'AC360' obtained the interview from Quade, who interviewed O'Neill over 18 months. O'Neill believes the killing of bin Laden will be a historical event. O'Neill remarked, 'But I don't care if I'm 'The Shooter,' and there are people who think I'm not. So whatever.' This audio interview followed a 'Washington Post' interview where O'Neill publicly identified himself as the SEAL who killed bin Laden in 2011. O'Neill, 38, previously shared mission details with 'Esquire' magazine but hesitated to attach his name until a military blog linked his identity to the story without his consent. O'Neill told 'The Washington Post' that other SEALs were involved, including Matt Bissonnette (pen name Mark Owen), who wrote about their experiences in 'No Easy Day'. O'Neill, a 15-year SEAL at the time, considered the bin Laden mission his most challenging. In the interview, O'Neill recalled SEAL Team Six members discussing the September 11, 2001, attacks and believing they wouldn't survive the bin Laden mission. 'Well, you have to go pump yourself up to go die. So we would talk about this,' O'Neill said. '...(It was a) group of guys who knew time on Earth was up, so you could be honest with each other. And we all accepted and nobody was afraid. It was really cool.' O'Neill also stated that families of 9/11 victims thanked him for closure after he identified himself as the shooter. 'He died afraid, and he knew we were there to kill him. And that's closure,' he said. O'Neill's public disclosure is controversial because it seemingly violates a military principle against seeking attention. A letter from Naval Special Warfare commanders B.L. Losey and M.L. Margaraci stated, 'We do not abide willful or selfish disregard for our core values in return for public notoriety or financial gain.' O'Neill argued that details of the bin Laden mission were declassified due to repeated leaks by high-level officials. 'Once anyone says anything at that level, it's not classified,' he said. '...I was told by people that I can't even say I'm a Navy SEAL, so I don't give a f*** what they think.' On May 2, 2011, twenty-three SEALs and their interpreter launched the assault on bin Laden's compound, killing bin Laden's bodyguards, one of his sons, and the wife of one bodyguard, while wounding two women. O'Neill previously shared his story in a 2013 'Esquire' profile as 'The Shooter'. The 'Esquire' piece described 'The Shooter' encountering bin Laden in a top-floor bedroom, where bin Laden had a gun 'within reach.' The Shooter then fired two shots into bin Laden's forehead. This account conflicts with 'No Easy Day.' Another SEAL Team 6 member told CNN that the 'Esquire' story was 'complete BS'. O'Neill dismissed the criticism, stating, 'Even now, I mean, there are guys now saying that I am full of s***,' '...You only know what you were told unless you were in the room. And unfortunately for me, there was two people in the room, and one of us is dead and that's Osama bin Laden.'

article_content: Devoted fans Theo Coyne, 28, and Lisa Potter-Coyne, 29, from London, took their admiration for R'n'B artist Craig David to an extraordinary level. They launched a social media campaign on Twitter and crafted a lighthearted YouTube video, both aimed at persuading David to attend their wedding. To their astonishment, and the delight of their guests and neighbors, the singer traveled approximately 1,500 miles to their reception held in the Cambridgeshire countryside, where he gave a performance. The couple's amusing four-minute video, showcasing Theo's rap tribute to their shared passion for Craig David's music, rapidly gained popularity, eventually capturing the singer's attention. David, 31, deeply touched by their attendance at over 25 of his concerts and the role his music played in strengthening their relationship, accepted their invitation. He was also moved by Theo's dedication to raising his younger brothers after their parents tragically died from cancer at a young age. Flying in from Los Angeles, David arrived at the rural Cambridgeshire home of Lisa's parents and treated the attendees to an hour-long performance in the garden. article_content: Timour Wielemans' £400 mountain bike was stolen two days before he was due to start university, leading him to believe he would never see it again. The 18-year-old faced a 90-minute walk home after the theft, which occurred on Wednesday, and had only one day left working in Cambridge before starting university in Warwick. However, the following day, while working his job selling punting tickets near where his bike had been stolen, he spotted a young man cycling past on his distinctive bike. Timour Wielemans, spotted the youth on his bike the day after it was stolen. While one of Timour's colleagues called the police, the Belgian student confronted the cyclist. Timour described the cyclist as 'not looking too clever but he did look pretty aggressive.' Instead of appearing nervous, the cyclist was casually talking on his mobile phone as he rode by. Timour recounted, 'I was selling tickets for the punts when I saw him. I was shocked, but then I knew I had to act. I dropped everything, ran after him, and stopped the bike. I asked him, 'Did you steal my bike?'' He likely didn't expect to be seen, especially only about 100 meters from where the bike was initially taken.' Colleagues from the punting company joined the chase and helped Timour retrieve his bike while one of them contacted the police. The student, originally from Belgium, commented, 'He didn't look too bright, but he seemed quite aggressive and angry. If my colleagues hadn't intervened, he might have hit me.' The man on the bike, who Timour described as 'quite angry,' was engaged in a phone call when he was recognized. A local photographer captured images of the suspected bike thief walking away from the scene. The student recovered his bike on the last day of his holiday job before heading off to university in Warwick. He pursued and confronted the thief with the support of his colleagues, who also alerted the police. The suspect escaped before the police arrived, but an officer stated she recognized the man in the photographs. Timour added, 'The PCSO initially thought it might be a similar bike, but upon seeing the pictures, she confirmed, 'Yep, he's a bike thief, that's definitely your bike.'' A spokesman for Cambridgeshire Police confirmed that enquiries into the incident are ongoing.

article_content: More than 60 children in Jamaica were hospitalized after consuming sweets containing cannabis, according to the country's education minister. Fayval Williams stated on X (formerly Twitter) that the primary school students were from the St Ann's Bay area, approximately 80km (50 miles) from Kingston, the capital. She reported that some children experienced vomiting and hallucinations, but none are in serious condition. 'The doctors and nurses are doing everything they can to ensure the students' recovery,' Williams wrote on X, noting that several children required intravenous (IV) drips. 'One little boy said he only ate ONE sweet. That's how potent this product is. DANGER!' Williams indicated the children attended St Ann's Bay Primary, but local news agencies suggest students from the nearby Ocho Rios Primary School were also affected. The children are believed to be between seven and 12 years old. The principal of St Ann's Bay Primary School informed the Jamaica Observer that a 'lone vendor' had sold the sweets to its students. Senior Superintendent Dwight Powell, head of the St Ann police department, has appealed for the vendor or anyone with information to contact the authorities. Williams shared photos of the product packaging, which stated that the sweets were not to be sold to minors. Each sweet is reported to contain 100mg of Delta-8 tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), a psychoactive substance, which is considered a high dose even for adults. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has stated that Delta-8 has 'intoxicating effects'. The sweets, which lack FDA approval, were produced by a California-based company, where cannabis is legal. Jamaica decriminalized the possession of small amounts of cannabis for personal use in 2015. However, Health Minister Christopher Tufton told the Jamaica Star that the government does not permit the import of edibles containing drugs. The incident occurred shortly after approximately 90 children in South Africa became ill after consuming drug-laced muffins purchased from a street vendor.

article_content: After her first evening out since the birth of her son, Flynn, actress Leigh Arnold returned home to a devastating scene. Her fiance, Steve Davies, was holding their lifeless son, who had stopped breathing after they both unintentionally fell asleep together on the sofa. Arnold, a well-known television personality in Ireland, had been encouraged by Davies to enjoy a relaxing dinner with a friend, a short respite from caring for their two-and-a-half-week-old infant. Upon arriving home, Arnold discovered Flynn 'grey' and unresponsive while Davies was still asleep. Despite immediate and desperate attempts by Davies and subsequently paramedics to resuscitate Flynn, he was pronounced dead at the hospital approximately one hour later. An inquest later confirmed that Flynn's death was due to Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), commonly referred to as cot death. Medical professionals who testified at the inquest assured the heartbroken parents that nothing more could have been done to prevent the tragedy. Arnold, recognized for her role as Dr. Clodagh Delaney in the Irish medical drama 'The Clinic', recounted collapsing in shock upon realizing her son's critical condition during the inquest. She described finding Flynn lying face up, with no apparent signs of being obstructed, yet visibly unwell. She expressed the immense love and adoration they had for Flynn, emphasizing how deeply he is missed. Arnold noted that Flynn had shown no prior symptoms of illness in the days leading up to his death and was contentedly feeding from a bottle on the night she went out. Davies explained that after dropping Arnold at the restaurant, he and Flynn made a quick trip to the supermarket before returning home, where their other son, Hunter, was being cared for by an au pair. Davies recalled falling asleep around 11 p.m. while holding Flynn, only to be abruptly awakened by Arnold's cries at 1:30 a.m. A police investigation following Flynn's death concluded that no one was at fault, and his death was unavoidable. Paediatrician Dr. Cate Lenton testified that Flynn was a 'perfect baby' and clarified that SIDS can occur even outside of a cot. Pathologist Dr. Gauri Batra attributed the cause of death as 'unascertained' but found no evidence of unnatural causes. Coroner Janet Napier extended her deepest condolences to the grieving couple, acknowledging the sudden and tragic nature of Flynn's passing and confirming it as a death by natural causes. The couple, who had to postpone their wedding last year due to Flynn's passing, are now planning to get married in Ibiza next month. Hunter, now two years old, will be the ring bearer. Arnold recently shared that she is taking things 'one day at a time' and is gradually considering returning to her acting career. She conveyed that it has been the most challenging period of her life and that she hopes to regain the confidence to pursue acting opportunities again. NHS guidelines advise parents to place babies on their backs to sleep in a cot and to avoid falling asleep with them on sofas or armchairs to reduce the risk of cot death.

article_content: A consultant for the Ministry of Defence (MoD) has been arrested because he's suspected of being involved with a website that offered to pay college tuition for female students in exchange for sexual encounters. The website, known as SponsorAScholar.co.uk, allegedly promised young women between the ages of 17 and 24 as much as £15,000 annually. The deal was for 'private escapades' with businessmen, taking place in apartments or hotel rooms. Mark Lancaster, a 39-year-old, was taken into custody in Milton Keynes. Authorities seized materials from both that location and his family residence in Horndean, close to Portsmouth. Lancaster, who had security clearance to work on a major MoD computer project, is suspected of encouraging prostitution, contributing to the growing problem of 'sex-for-fees' arrangements. He was questioned by police and then released on bail. He's expected to return to Charing Cross police station in London in February. The arrest came after The Independent conducted an undercover investigation focusing on a man claiming to be an 'assessor' for the website. An undercover reporter, pretending to be a student, met with the 'assessor' at a McDonald's in south London two weeks prior. She was informed that she would need to participate in a 'practical assessment' with him at a nearby apartment. This assessment was supposedly to evaluate how comfortable she was with intimacy, which would determine her suitability for future 'sponsors'. She was also told that it was her choice whether or not to use protection during encounters with these men. The reporter secretly recorded the encounter, declined the assessment, and left. Since then, the SponsorAScholar.co.uk website has been shut down. The website used pictures of women and claimed to have positive reviews from users. The website claimed that 1,400 women had received 'scholarships,' but there's no confirmation on how many women actually contacted the site or if any money was ever exchanged. Jo Swinson, the Minister for Women, had previously urged the police to investigate anyone thought to be exploiting students. The website described its sponsors as 'men between 28 and 50 years old who are successful business owners seeking discreet adventures with students while helping them with their education through scholarships'. It even suggested that the scholarship amount was tax deductible. In November, an undercover reporter from Channel 4 News interviewed the man behind the website at a rented apartment in southeast London. Although he identified himself as John, the news organization believed it was Lancaster. One student told Channel 4 News that she underwent the 'practical assessment' and was later informed via email that her application was unsuccessful. However, she was told she could reapply in two months. The 'assessor' used the name and former address of a leading academic from a prominent British university when communicating with potential students. The academic has since contacted the police. Minister for Women Jo Swinson urged the police to investigate anyone suspected of taking advantage of students. The investigation follows rising worries that increasing student fees might be pushing young individuals into sex work to pay off their debts. Experts suggested that SponsorAScholar.co.uk was just the 'tip of the iceberg'. Detective Sergeant Alan Clark encouraged anyone who had contacted the website to reach out to the police. 'If you have information related to the man in the film, photos, or on the website, please contact us on 0800 783 2589, and we assure you that it will be treated confidentially,' he stated. Lancaster had the necessary clearance to work on the MoD's extensive 'DII' or Defence Information Infrastructure contract, which aimed to consolidate the military's various computer networks.

article_content: Alan Yentob defended his £330,000 salary while also expressing concerns about the high salaries paid to top BBC stars. Known to some colleagues as ‘Two-Jobs’ due to his multiple BBC roles, Alan Yentob, like some of the corporation’s biggest stars, feels uneasy with the large sums of money paid to top talent. The 66-year-old executive, who earns around £333,000 annually as the BBC’s creative director and arts presenter, admitted feeling that the ‘huge amounts of money’ given to presenters like Graham Norton and Gary Lineker were unfair. During a panel discussion at the Radio Academy’s festival in Salford, which was broadcast on Radio 5 Live, Yentob responded to listener Chris Jones's complaint about feeling ‘betrayed’ by high BBC pay, and also objected to the significant earnings of Premiership footballers such as Wayne Rooney. Jones stated that the disparity between the high salaries of stars and the average public earning of around £25,000 was unfair, citing Graham Norton and Gary Lineker as examples at the BBC. While Graham Norton and Gary Lineker are thought to earn about £1.5 million each year at the BBC, Wayne Rooney earns an estimated £15.6 million a year from Manchester United and commercial endorsements. Yentob defended BBC salaries by claiming they were lower than those at ITV, but agreed with Jones regarding the earnings of Wayne Rooney and presenters, including himself and Richard Bacon. Yentob justified his own pay by asserting his ‘value’ to the BBC through his ‘relationship with talent’ and ‘understanding of the networks and the schedules.’ He receives one salary of £183,300 as BBC creative director and another as editor and presenter of Imagine. Although Yentob has not disclosed the amount of his additional income, BBC insiders estimate it to be around £150,000 a year. He has also accumulated a pension pot of £6 million. Yentob also defended Jeremy Clarkson's earnings, noting that Top Gear generates significant revenue for the BBC through BBC Worldwide, which exceeds Clarkson's compensation. The BBC has faced heavy criticism for its expenditure on executive salaries. Last month, MPs questioned seven managers who collectively earned £1.6 million a year. Mark Thompson, former director general, earned £670,000 a year, while Lucy Adams, human resources director, received a salary of £320,000. The broadcasters had also hired executives on salaries exceeding £200,000 in the past year. A 2009 BBC Trust study found basic salaries comparable to those at top FTSE 100 companies. Salaries of key BBC executives include: Tony Hall, director general (£450,000); Anne Bulford, managing director (£395,000); Helen Boaden, director of radio (£340,000); James Harding, director of news (£340,000); Danny Cohen, director of television (£327,800); James Purnell, director of strategy (£295,000); and Lord Patten, BBC Trust Chairman (£110,000).

article_content: Two language specialists have voiced their disappointment and concern over criticism directed at former rugby star Mike Phillips regarding his Welsh language proficiency. Their support comes after a TV executive was dismissed from S4C, the Welsh language channel, following allegations that she verbally disparaged Phillips' Welsh at the Rugby World Cup. Reportedly, Llinos Griffin-Williams, the former chief content officer at S4C, suggested that Phillips' Welsh wasn't up to par. S4C has emphasized that promoting the Welsh language is central to their mission, and they consider the former player a crucial part of their broadcasting team. Sources indicate that Ms. Griffin-Williams also hinted at the possibility of impacting Phillips' career as a presenter. Information suggests that Ms. Griffin-Williams was present in Nantes in an official capacity during the Wales versus Georgia Rugby World Cup match. Another alleged incident occurred at a different bar in the city. On BBC Radio Cymru's 'Bore Sul' program, Gwyn Williams, chief officer of the professional body for Welsh/English translation, and Helen Prosser, director of teaching and learning at the National Centre for Learning Welsh, both offered their support to Phillips. Phillips, whose first language is Welsh, hails from a farming family in Bancyfelin, Carmarthenshire, and earned 94 caps for Wales. 'I had the opportunity to watch the live coverage last night and thought Mike Phillips performed exceptionally well,' stated Mr. Williams. 'He contributed his knowledge, his experience, and a good dose of humor. While perfect Welsh is desirable, it's not always realistic. I prefer relaxed Welsh over polished English. This situation is unfortunate and embarrassing.' Phillips has been involved with S4C's coverage of the Rugby World Cup in France. Mr. Williams expressed concern that this incident might negatively affect the confidence of other Welsh learners. He drew parallels to previous criticism aimed at John Hartson's Welsh on the S4C program 'Sgorio'. Mr. Williams noted that Phillips had recently voiced concerns about his Welsh, particularly because he resides in Dubai, where maintaining Welsh proficiency can be challenging. He questioned the impact of such criticism on less confident Welsh learners, especially if it affects individuals with a strong public profile. Furthermore, an independent external investigation was initiated in May into the publicly funded channel following claims of a 'bullying and toxic culture'. The Broadcasting, Entertainment, Communications and Theatre Union (Bectu) reported a 'culture of fear' within the organization. Mr. Williams confirmed that he provided evidence to the investigation conducted by Capital Law and awaits its publication. Expressing her regret over the extensive attention the issue received, particularly during Celebrating Learning Welsh Week, Ms. Prosser also lauded the former player's Welsh as 'lovely' and 'natural'. She noted her appreciation for the widespread support Phillips has received. An S4C spokesperson affirmed that encouraging and promoting the use of Welsh is fundamental to S4C's operations. They highlighted the positive reception of their Rugby World Cup coverage, emphasizing Mike Phillips' integral role. BBC Wales has reached out to both Ms. Griffin-Williams and the former rugby player for their responses.

article_content: If Kanye West had his way, flesh-toned body stockings might be the next big trend. Despite how unusual it sounds, the musician-turned-designer has garnered praise from fashion editors, authorities, and influencers for his Adidas collection. The collection debuted at New York Fashion Week, featuring full body stockings, see-through skin-colored crop tops, and visible nude pants, presenting a new take on underwear as outerwear that's not for the faint of heart. Scroll down for a video. Deni Kirkova, 24, from London, tested a makeshift version of the outfits seen on the Kanye West X Adidas catwalk on a London High Street. The Kanye West Adidas Fall 2015 collection received acclaim from fashion's elite, but does the public agree it's a fashionable look? To gain recognition for his fashion line is a significant step for Kanye. Femail is exploring whether his clothing will resonate with the public. Writer Deni Kirkova, 24, from London, experimented with the full flesh-colored body stocking look, venturing onto a London High Street to gauge reactions. She combined an American Apparel bralet (£12.50), crop top (£10), leggings (£14), and a £6 pair of Marks & Spencer pants worn over the top, all in a beige flesh tone, complemented by a Kim K-style parka jacket from Topshop. Regarding her outfit and its impact, Deni commented: 'The visible pants are the issue. It's amusing to walk around dressed like this, but I wouldn't wear this look seriously. A nude crop top and leggings, however, could work. It would need to be toned down to transition from the catwalk to everyday wear. I'm surprised that people generally liked my outfit; some fashion enthusiasts praised its boldness, noting the Kanye influence and the harmony between the jacket and lipstick. Of course, some felt the pants were excessive.' Deni paired an American Apparel bralet, crop top, and leggings with M&S pants worn on top, all in beige, and a parka. Deni's look drew inspiration from the Adidas Originals x Kanye West Yeezy collection showcased in New York on Thursday. Kanye's wife, Kim Kardashian, 34, attended wearing an ensemble from the collection. She appreciated the look so much that she shared an Instagram photo, adding: 'My look for the Yeezy show!!!!!! Yeezy head to toe!!!!!' Critics also seemed to appreciate Kanye's fashion efforts, with Vogue stating: 'Kanye West's New collection with Adidas lives up to the hype.' Editor-in-chief Anna Wintour and designer Alexander Wang were seated in the front row. Kim Kardashian wore a brown body stocking with a grey crop top and a camo jacket. From builders to couples, fashionistas to older women, the bold look seemed to be well-received, much to Deni's surprise. The main issue for Deni was the visible pants. 'It's amusing to walk around dressed like this now, but I wouldn't wear it seriously.' A review on the fashion magazine's website noted: 'Hems were raw and frayed, tops billowy, bottoms either skintight, to be worn with new suede stiletto boots, or cinched. There were flak vests and officer sweaters that appeared combat-worn, and everything was supposedly unisex... The collection, presented by rigid lines of expressionless youth, was at least satisfyingly provocative for sportswear.' Refinery 29 noted the potential for strong sales: 'It was a collection of oversized jackets, sweatshirts, sweaters, and leggings, along with Vanessa Beecroft-esque nude-colored underwear. A camo parka, also worn by Kim Kardashian, stood out, and the oversized backpack was a clever accessory likely to feature in numerous editorials.' Kanye stated that he wanted the collection to offer 'solutions-based clothing,' adding, 'I don't want the clothes to be the life; I want the clothes to enhance the life.' The collection is expected to be priced lower than other designer items, making it accessible to his fans. Now that the fully nude, spray-on look has gained approval from fashion insiders and the public, will you try it? Deni suggests a nude crop top and leggings could be a viable option, without the pants, if toned down. The show marks the first time Kanye has received praise for his fashion designs. Kanye's collection included baggy coats worn over body stockings. Models stood in an army-like formation, showcasing the outfits designed by the rapper.

article_content: Former Conservative chief whip Andrew Mitchell has launched a scathing attack on Downing Street and Scotland Yard, criticizing David Cameron's judgment and the impartiality of Met Commissioner Bernard Hogan-Howe. This attack comes as the Police Federation, which represents rank-and-file officers, has ordered a review into its handling of the 'plebgate' episode. The Federation has been accused of fueling the controversy surrounding Mitchell's alleged outburst, which ultimately led to his resignation from the Cabinet. Police Federation chairman Paul McKeever stated he would apologize to Mitchell if it were proven that he did not call police officers 'plebs'. The Federation vocally opposed Mitchell's alleged behavior, with some branches organizing protests where officers wore 'PC Pleb' t-shirts. Friends of the former chief whip expressed disbelief that the Prime Minister allowed Mitchell to resign, despite knowing that CCTV footage cast significant doubt on the police's claims that Mitchell called them 'plebs'. Mitchell's allies claim he wasn't even allowed to view the video before his resignation and was instead left 'swinging in the wind'. Tory MPs have also called for the suspension of the two diplomatic protection officers whose log made the claims, pending a criminal investigation into the events of last September. The CCTV footage shows Mitchell being denied access through the Downing Street gates but does not depict the alleged heated argument or the 'visibly shocked' members of the public the police claimed were present. Mitchell admits to swearing but denies using the word 'plebs'. Up to 30 Scotland Yard detectives are investigating after it emerged that a third policeman falsely posed as a member of the public and claimed to have witnessed the incident in an email to Tory deputy chief whip John Randall. Cameron and Cabinet Secretary Sir Jeremy Heywood reviewed the footage and concluded it undermined the email. However, the Prime Minister chose not to confront the police and, crucially, did not show the video to Mitchell for his defense. A close friend of Mitchell described the situation in Downing Street as 'amateur hour', emphasizing their disbelief that crucial evidence was withheld. The source questioned Cameron's judgment, arguing that prioritizing the avoidance of upsetting the police over releasing exculpatory evidence was 'mindblowing'. The source also agreed that the two police officers who made the original claim should be suspended pending the investigation's results. Another Tory MP echoed this sentiment, highlighting the clear discrepancies between the police account and the CCTV footage and suggesting the officers have a case to answer. Mitchell's allies have also indicated his lack of faith in the impartiality of Met Commissioner Bernard Hogan-Howe, particularly after Hogan-Howe stated that the CCTV evidence did not contradict the police log. However, Mitchell has been reassured by Scotland Yard's decision to put deputy assistant commissioner Pat Gallan in charge of the investigation. CCTV footage from Downing Street, as shown on Channel 4 News, suggests that there was no group of tourists present at the gates during the incident. Downing Street declined to comment on when Mitchell was given the video but noted that the Prime Minister stood by him for several weeks after the incident, despite persistent calls for his dismissal. Cameron and London Mayor Boris Johnson both voiced their support for Hogan-Howe. A Downing Street spokesman stated that the Prime Minister has full confidence in the Metropolitan police commissioner and believes the police should be allowed to conduct the investigation. Johnson's spokesman affirmed the Mayor's absolute confidence in the commissioner, who has assured him of his determination to resolve the matter quickly. Cameron revealed that he met privately with Mitchell the previous week and had been eager to retain him in his position. Mitchell's allies suggest he would readily accept his old job of International Development Secretary back in a reshuffle. During his visit to Afghanistan, Cameron expressed sympathy for Mitchell, citing the shock caused by the revelation of the email. He mentioned speaking with Mitchell on Monday, describing him as being in a 'calm and rational mood' despite the 'disturbing revelations'. Keith Vaz, Labour chairman of the Commons Home Affairs Committee, announced that Hogan-Howe will answer questions about the affair on January 14. Police Federation chief Paul McKeever has handed control to his successor-elect Steve Williams, just over a month before his official departure, due to 'pre-existing leave arrangements'. Announcing a review of the body, he stated that recent events have highlighted issues regarding the Police Federation's ability to lead and coordinate effectively at various levels. He continued, 'As we enter a new era, my first act as chairman is to establish this independent panel to ensure that we as the Federation continue to represent the interests of our members in the most effective and efficient way.'

article_content: The search for two American climbers in the Peruvian mountains concluded on Saturday afternoon with the discovery of their bodies, according to statements from their friends and family. Ben Horne and Gil Weiss were attempting to climb the south face of Palcaraju Oeste, a 6,110-meter peak in Huaraz province, a popular climbing destination roughly 275 miles northeast of Lima. Shay Har-Noy, who leads the satellite imagery firm Tomnod, remembered Horne and Weiss as exceptional climbers who embodied the spirit of mountaineering. Tomnod's website expressed that many individuals had the privilege of sharing in their passion for the wilderness, which would continue to live on. Weiss, the founder of Beyond Adventure, had announced his departure for another season in the High Andes on his Facebook page on June 11. Horne had documented their climbing experiences on the blog Pullharder.org on July 10, praising the Cordillera Blanca for its high-altitude mountaineering and the diverse group of international climbers it attracts. According to Tomnod, Weiss and Horne had been missing for five to ten days. Kari Tenjford, a friend, mentioned on Facebook that the search team located the climbers' tent and tracks on the glacier and descent ridge. Har-Noy mobilized climbers and technology experts, utilizing an application he developed, where hundreds analyzed satellite images for avalanche signs. This information was then relayed to Peruvian search and rescue teams. Another friend, Asa Firestone, reported that the climbers' bodies were found following a fall from the southwest ridge during their descent. Firestone remembered Horne and Weiss as amazing individuals who shared their passion for adventure through their blog and groundbreaking ascents. Har-Noy noted that Horne and Weiss were highly experienced climbers with over a decade of practice. While Weiss had visited Peru previously, this was Horne's first trip. Gil's sister, Galit Weiss, conveyed her love for Gil and how he would continue to inspire her.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- Senate Republicans and Democrats agreed Thursday that they would prefer a new education bill to the current use of waivers by the Obama administration. These waivers bypass the No Child Left Behind Act, which is more than five years overdue for an overhaul. 'The bottom line is that it expired in 2007, but a provision allowed it to continue if Congress didn't act. Congress didn't act, so it's continuing,' said Sen. Lamar Alexander, R-Tennessee, the ranking Republican on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee. 'That's our fault. That's on us,' Alexander added. Education Secretary Arne Duncan appeared before the committee to provide an update on his use of waivers for states unable to meet the criteria outlined in the No Child Left Behind Act. These waivers allow states to continue receiving federal education funding until Congress reauthorizes the program. 'Providing waivers was always our plan B. I was not willing to stand idly by while students and educators continue to suffer under No Child Left Behind,' the secretary said. The waivers have been controversial among Republicans who object to the stipulations the Obama administration places on states before awarding them. 'This simple waiver authority has turned into a conditional waiver. The secretary basically has more authority to make decisions that, in my view, should be made locally by state and local governments,' Alexander said. If Congress agrees on a deal to reauthorize NCLB, which is the current version of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA), Duncan believes the waivers would become obsolete. According to the education secretary, 34 states and the District of Columbia have been granted waivers. Nine states, Puerto Rico, and the Bureau of Indian Education have requests under consideration. The deadline to apply for the waivers is the end of February. During the last Congress, a bill from the Senate committee to reauthorize ESEA died at the end of the session without reaching the Senate floor for debate. Several smaller bills addressing ESEA topics were passed out of the House Committee on Education and the Workforce last year. One of those bills, dealing with Charter Schools, passed the House but died at the end of the last session due to inaction in the Senate. 'It's no secret that Congress has been dysfunctional for many years,' Duncan said. 'My team and I put in hundreds of hours in what proved to be a fruitless effort over the past two years. In all candor, I would have preferred to implement waivers earlier.'

article_content: The world's response to Ebola is a tragedy. Two key facts highlight this: The United Nations requested $1 billion to combat the virus's spread, but as of Friday, only $100,000 (0.01%) had been collected. An additional $20 million has been pledged but not yet received, according to CNN Money. 'We need to turn pledges into action,' U.N. Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon stated. 'We require more doctors, nurses, equipment, and treatment centers.' Liberia, the nation hardest hit by Ebola, reports needing 2.4 million boxes of protective gloves and 85,000 body bags to effectively fight the virus over the next six months. Currently, they possess only 18,000 boxes of gloves and fewer than 5,000 body bags. Consider the significance of needing 85,000 body bags. What truly underlies the international community's insufficient assistance? Some U.S. commentators blame Obama, likening it to his 'Katrina moment,' but these critiques are more related to upcoming elections. Obama's Friday announcement of an 'Ebola czar' is unlikely to silence them. However, the real devastation has been unfolding in West Africa for months, yet it elicits less outrage in the United States. Kofi Annan, former U.N. Secretary-General from Ghana, recently told the BBC that 'If the crisis had occurred in another region, it probably would have been handled differently. The international community truly took notice when the disease reached America and Europe.' It's difficult to deny that race and geography influence the world's indifference, explaining why 'some other region' would receive more support. Research indicates lighter-skinned individuals struggle to 'feel' the pain of darker-skinned individuals. A University of Milano-Bicocca study showed Caucasian participants videos of people of various races being pricked with a needle. The white viewers showed greater physical empathy when white people were hurt compared to Africans. Another study, as Slate reported, found white participants, black participants, and nurses assumed blacks felt less pain than whites. With the exception of a few health workers, nearly all of Ebola's 4,400 victims have been black Africans, revealing troubling biases. Hannah Giorgis wrote in The Guardian that 'Ebola is now a stand-in for any combination of African-ness, blackness, foreign-ness, and infestation – poised to ruin the perceived purity of Western borders and bodies.' This pattern has a long, disturbing history, as seen in the 1994 Rwanda genocide and the HIV/AIDS epidemic. John Ashton, president of the UK Faculty of Public Health, noted in The Independent, 'In the case of AIDS, proper research funding was delayed until so-called 'innocent' groups (women, children, hemophiliacs, and straight men) were affected.' His headline read: 'They'd find a cure if Ebola came to London.' Geography also plays a role. Americans are often ignorant about Africa (test yourself with the Washington Post's African geography quiz). The physical distance between Africa and financial/political centers in North America and Europe can foster emotional detachment. A friend wrote, 'I don't know about racism, but when Ebola was confined to Africa, few in the U.S. cared about the thousands dying. Now that a few have it in the U.S., there's widespread panic.' Regardless of the cause, a lack of empathy is evident. Too many panic when Ebola appears in Dallas but ignore the grim situation in Monrovia. Too many worry about potential Ebola exposure on a cruise to Belize but disregard Ebola's orphaned children. Highlighting these realities can spur change. Leslie Jamison, a former 'medical actor' who faked illnesses for medical students, learned about empathy. 'Empathy isn't just an event – it's a choice: to pay attention, to extend ourselves,' she wrote. Accept this challenge: Pay attention, extend yourself, and demand action from world leaders.
